comparison: First-principles analyst-reviewed assignment crosswalk: ICASSP 2026 and INTERSPEECH 2025

evidence_depth.icassp: D1 title-only for records without abstract; D2 abstract-supported for 683 records; discovery metadata rather than official proceedings.
evidence_depth.interspeech: D2 official archive paper pages and abstracts; D3 full-paper evidence currently covers 122 captured papers.

crosswalk.theme_name: Listening through noise, overlap, and missing sound
From sound to words and structured speech
From spoken form to meaning and coordinated action
Creating speech while keeping the right things fixed
Speakers as changing people, not nuisance variables
Many languages, accents, and unequal evidence

conceptual_contrasts.label: Mixtures and competing speakers
conceptual_contrasts.ordinary_problem: A listener or recognizer must decide which voice belongs to which person when speech overlaps.

interspeech.title: ReSepNet: A Unified-Light Model for Recursive Speech Separation with Unknown Speaker Count
interspeech.semantic_reasoning: Recursive separation makes the unknown speaker count part of the separation problem.

icassp.title: Loose Coupling of Spectral and Spatial Models for Multi-Channel Diarization and Enhancement of Meetings in Dynamic Environments
icassp.semantic_reasoning: Meeting diarization and enhancement must use spectral and spatial evidence together when speakers and room conditions change.

conceptual_contrasts.denominator_statement: INTERSPEECH comparison context is the 1,179-record archive corpus; ICASSP comparison context is the 3,864-record captured corpus, with this named contrast using one reviewed paper from each venue.
conceptual_contrasts.conceptual_difference: INTERSPEECH makes unknown speaker count the central structural problem and recursively peels voices apart; the reviewed ICASSP paper treats meeting diarization and enhancement as coupled spatial decisions in a changing room.
conceptual_contrasts.evidence_boundary: INTERSPEECH is D3 full-paper evidence; ICASSP is D2 abstract evidence, so this is a mechanism contrast, not a venue prevalence claim.

conceptual_contrasts.label: Recognition and usable boundaries
conceptual_contrasts.ordinary_problem: Recognizing words is not enough if the system cannot decide when a unit is complete or how it becomes usable text.

interspeech.title: Dynamic Context-Aware Streaming Pretrained Language Model For Inverse Text Normalization
interspeech.semantic_reasoning: Streaming inverse text normalization makes the recognition-to-written-text boundary explicit under limited context and latency.

icassp.title: Scale: Semantic Chunking and Label-Delay Engine For Streaming Speech-LLM
icassp.semantic_reasoning: Streaming speech models need explicit chunk and label-delay rules to trade context against response time.

conceptual_contrasts.denominator_statement: INTERSPEECH comparison context is the 1,179-record archive corpus; ICASSP comparison context is the 3,864-record captured corpus, with this named contrast using one reviewed paper from each venue.
conceptual_contrasts.conceptual_difference: INTERSPEECH uses dynamic right-context and chunk size for streaming inverse text normalization; the ICASSP title-bounded assignment concerns semantic chunking and label delay inside a speech-language stream.
conceptual_contrasts.evidence_boundary: The INTERSPEECH mechanism is D3; the ICASSP assignment is D1 title evidence and cannot support outcome or mechanism detail.

conceptual_contrasts.label: Emotion as interactional evidence
conceptual_contrasts.ordinary_problem: Emotion is not a fixed label in the waveform; it is inferred from changing cues, missing channels, and listener interpretation.

interspeech.title: Label Semantic-Driven Contrastive Learning for Speech Emotion Recognition
interspeech.semantic_reasoning: Emotion labels are not equally separated in speech; label semantics are used as anchors for subtle affective distinctions.

icassp.title: SURE: Synergistic Uncertainty-aware Reasoning for Multimodal Emotion Recognition in Conversations
icassp.semantic_reasoning: Emotion recognition in conversation needs uncertainty-aware reasoning because affect and context are not fixed independent labels.

conceptual_contrasts.denominator_statement: INTERSPEECH comparison context is the 1,179-record archive corpus; ICASSP comparison context is the 3,864-record captured corpus, with this named contrast using one reviewed paper from each venue.
conceptual_contrasts.conceptual_difference: INTERSPEECH uses label semantics as anchors for subtle emotion boundaries; the ICASSP paper frames uncertainty-aware reasoning over multimodal conversation as the way to handle ambiguous evidence.
conceptual_contrasts.evidence_boundary: Both are abstract-bounded D2 assignments here; neither establishes general emotional understanding or comparable performance across venues.

conceptual_contrasts.label: Creating speech while preserving identity
conceptual_contrasts.ordinary_problem: A speech generator must change the requested content or style without accidentally changing who is speaking or how understandable the result is.

interspeech.title: Bridging the Training–Inference Gap in TTS: Training Strategies for Robust Generative Postprocessing for Low-Resource Speakers
interspeech.semantic_reasoning: Generative postprocessing improves low-resource TTS naturalness while checking objective proxies against listener judgments.

icassp.title: F5E-TTS: Enhancing Speech Synthesis by Aligning Text with Rich Semantic Representations
icassp.semantic_reasoning: Speech synthesis must align semantic text content with the acoustic sequence so fluent wording does not drift from what is spoken.

conceptual_contrasts.denominator_statement: INTERSPEECH comparison context is the 1,179-record archive corpus; ICASSP comparison context is the 3,864-record captured corpus, with this named contrast using one reviewed paper from each venue.
conceptual_contrasts.conceptual_difference: INTERSPEECH separates low-resource TTS generation from a naturalness postprocessor and checks listener judgments; the ICASSP abstract assignment focuses on aligning text with rich semantic representations during synthesis.
conceptual_contrasts.evidence_boundary: The INTERSPEECH result is D3 and author-reported; the ICASSP comparison is D2 abstract evidence, so quality and mechanism are not directly comparable.

comparability_boundaries: Counts are analyst-reviewed primary-candidate assignments, not prevalence estimates.
A paper can have multiple candidate subthemes; the table uses only the highest-scoring candidate for a compact comparison.
ICASSP contains a broad non-speech corpus; unsupported rows remain in its denominator rather than being discarded.
ICASSP title-only records cannot support abstract-level mechanism or outcome claims.
INTERSPEECH abstracts are available for all records, but only 122 papers currently have captured full-paper D3 notes.
